newsitem.title: UK: UK financial sector profits up, optimism muted-CBI.
newsitem.headline: UK financial sector profits up, optimism muted-CBI.

text.p: Britain's financial services sector posted a strong rise in profitability over the three months to June as volume of business rose steadily, the Confederation of British Industry said on Monday.
But business optimism, although it rose, did so at a slower rate than at any time since December 1995.

The CBI's quarterly survey showed 50 percent of the 247 companies canvassed said profits had risen while only 15 percent reported a fall -- a positive balance of 35 percent, up from 23 percent in March.

"This is a positive survey with Britain's financial services on the up with a strong rise in profitability, above-expected increases in employment and a healthy rise in business volumes," said Sudhir Junankar, the CBI's associate director of economic analysis.

But he conceded that confidence within the sector was muted. A positive balance of 20 percent of firms said they were optimistic about their business situation, down from 26 percent in March and 61 percent in December 1996.

"This could be due to the impact of domestic competition which companies say is still the most likely constraint on business prospects over the coming year, closely followed by the level of demand, which has risen significantly as a constraint since the last survey," Junankar said.
Employment in financial services increased by a positive balance of six percent, more than was expected in the last survey. But in March, the employment balance was plus 11 percent.
Volume of business posted a positive balance of 40 percent but that was well below the 79 percent seen in last December's survey.
Investment in information technology is expected to grow strongly in the year ahead, with intentions most buoyant since the survey began in 1989.

"There is still plenty of room for optimism in the financial services sector, but there is no room for complacency," said Pat Newberry, a partner in Coopers & Lybrand's Financial Services Consulting Practice.
"The number of competitors and the level of domestic demand continue to be of concern, especially in the banking and general insurance sectors."
The CBI produces its financial services survey in conjunction with Coopers & Lybrand.
